name: @zaisma/lighting
summary: Lighting and sky for three.js: a sky with sun, moon, stars and clouds, sunlight whose shadows follow the player, fill light, reflections and fog that match the sky (glowing toward a low sun, and pooling low as ground fog), all set by the time of day, with quality that fits every device from a phone up.

settings.name: time_of_day_hours
settings.summary: The time of day, from 0 to 24: the sun rises at 6, is highest at 12 and sets at 18. While day_length_min is above 0 it moves on its own, and setting it jumps there.

settings.name: day_length_min
settings.summary: How many real minutes a whole day takes, so the sun crosses the sky while playing; 0 keeps the time where it's set.

settings.name: sun_peak_elevation_deg
settings.summary: How high the sun climbs at noon, in degrees above the horizon: lower gives long shadows all day, 90 passes straight overhead.

settings.name: sun_path_turn_deg
settings.summary: Turns the sun's path round the up axis, in degrees counterclockwise seen from above, to choose which way shadows fall. At 0 the sun rises toward +x and is highest toward +z.

settings.name: quality_level
settings.summary: How much the lighting draws. low: no shadows, reflections or clouds, for the weakest phones. medium: shadows, reflections and clouds. high: sharper, soft-edged shadows. auto starts at what the device can carry (medium on phones and tablets, high elsewhere) and steps down while frames run slow.

settings.name: shadows_enabled
settings.summary: Whether the sun casts shadows at medium quality and above. Things cast and take shadows once the game passes them to giveShadows, or sets castShadow and receiveShadow itself.

settings.name: shadow_distance_m
settings.summary: How far the sun's shadows reach round what they follow, in metres: smaller is sharper, larger reaches further.

settings.name: light_strength_pct
settings.summary: How strong the sun (or the moon at night) is, against the time of day's own strength.

settings.name: fill_strength_pct
settings.summary: How strong the light from the sky and the ground is, which lights what the sun doesn't reach, against the time of day's own strength.

settings.name: reflections_enabled
settings.summary: Whether three's standard and physical materials reflect the sky and are lit by it, at medium quality and above, so metal and shiny surfaces look right.

settings.name: exposure_pct
settings.summary: How bright the whole picture is, as a camera's exposure.

settings.name: tone_mapping
settings.summary: How bright light is fitted to the screen. neutral keeps the colours a game picks; aces is a filmic look with deeper contrast; agx softens bright colours toward white; none leaves three's output as it is.

settings.name: fog_enabled
settings.summary: Whether far things fade into the sky's colour, so the world's edge is never a hard line.

settings.name: fog_start_m
settings.summary: How far from the camera the fog starts, in metres.

settings.name: fog_end_m
settings.summary: How far from the camera the fog hides everything, in metres. Keep it inside the camera's far distance.

settings.name: fog_sun_glow_pct
settings.summary: How warmly the fog glows toward the sun while it's low, at sunrise and sunset, in the sun's own colour: 0 keeps the fog one colour all round.

settings.name: ground_fog_pct
settings.summary: How thick the fog pooling low over the ground is, a valley's mist or a marsh's: 0 is none, 100 hides the ground 50 metres away. It's in the fog's colour, and shows with fog_enabled off too.

settings.name: ground_fog_height_m
settings.summary: How high the ground fog reaches, in metres: it thins by two thirds each this far up from its floor.

settings.name: ground_fog_floor_m
settings.summary: The height the ground fog lies on, in metres, where it's thickest: the ground's height, or a valley's floor.

settings.name: clouds_pct
settings.summary: How much of the sky the clouds cover: 0 is clear, 100 overcast. Clouds drift slowly, and are left out at low quality.

settings.name: stars_enabled
settings.summary: Whether stars and the moon show in the night sky.

hooks.name: before_look
hooks.summary: Asked whenever the time of day or a setting changes the look, with every colour and strength: { zenithColor, horizonColor, fogColor, lightColor, lightLux, fillSkyColor, fillGroundColor, fillLux, cloudColor, starsPct }, colours as "#rrggbb". Answer a look with any of them changed (a storm, an alien sky, a cave), or nothing to leave it.

hooks.name: day_started
hooks.summary: Told when the sun comes up and lights the scene again, with the time of day in hours.

hooks.name: night_started
hooks.summary: Told when the sun goes down far enough that the moon lights the scene, with the time of day in hours.

hooks.name: quality_changed
hooks.summary: Told when the quality level in use changes, with { qualityLevel, reason }: reason is setting, or slow_frames when auto stepped down because frames ran slow.
